title: Plural 5: Dative (-ам / -ям)
description: After the difficulty of the plural genitive, the plural dative is a relief. One ending across all three genders, written -ам after hard stems and -ям after soft stems. Triggered by помогать, к + dat, по + dat (habitual), and the other dative-taking verbs you already know.
descriptionRussian: После сложного родительного падежа дательный падеж множественного числа — это передышка. Одно окончание для всех трёх родов: -ам после твёрдых основ и -ям после мягких. Используется с помогать, к, по и другими дательными конструкциями.
intro: From here the book gets easier and stays easier. Gender stops mattering: one ending covers masculine, feminine and neuter, and the only choice left is whether the stem is hard or soft. After two lessons of genitive, that should feel like being let out of somewhere.
rules: The plural dative has one ending across all three genders. Hard stems take -ам; soft stems take -ям.
Hard stems (-ам): hard masc cons (журналам), hard fem -а (книгам), hard neuter -о (окнам), ж ш ч щ (карандашам, врачам), velars к г х (девочкам).
Soft stems (-ям): soft masc -й (музеям), soft masc -ь (учителям), soft fem -я (песням), soft fem -ь (тетрадям), soft neuter -е (морям).
Family-plural masculines take -ьям: братьям, друзьям, сыновьям, стульям. Suppletive plurals take the regular soft ending on the suppletive stem: детям, людям.
Triggers: помогать, звонить, писать, посылать, дарить, рассказывать + dat; к + dat (motion toward people); по + dat pl (habitual: по утрам, по выходным); нравиться + dat; рад + dat.

Spelling note: a feminine -ь ending in ж ш щ ч ц takes -ам (not -ям) by the 7-letter rule: ночь → ночам. Separately, дочь extends its stem before the ending, which places a soft consonant р in front of it, so it takes -ям: дочь → дочерям.
examples: Маша часто помогает друзьям. (Masha often helps her friends.) друг → друзьям, family-pl + -ьям.
Антон идёт к друзьям. (Anton is going to his friends'.) к + dat pl: друзьям.
Лена работает по утрам. (Lena works in the mornings.) по + dat pl habit: утро → утрам.
Учитель помогает девочкам. (The teacher is helping the girls.) девочка → девочкам, velar к → -ам.
Маша рассказывает истории детям. (Masha is telling the children stories.) ребёнок → дети → детям, different-word plural + -ям.
Антон пишет письма братьям. (Anton is writing letters to his brothers.) брат → братьям, family-pl + -ьям.

items.promptEnglish: There are many books in the library.
items.hint: Recap from L4: hard fem -а stems take which gen pl ending after много?
items.explanation: L4 recap: hard fem -а drops the -а to a zero ending in the gen pl: книга → книг. After много + countable plural, the noun is in the genitive plural. Today's lesson moves to the dative plural, which is much simpler.

items.hint: Помогать takes the dative. Брат belongs to the -ья family. What is the dat pl?
items.explanation: Помогать + dative is one of the core dative triggers. Брат takes the family-plural pattern, so the dat pl is братьям. Other family-pl masculines follow the same rule: друзьям, сыновьям, стульям.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is going to his friends'.
items.hint: К takes the dative. Друг belongs to the -ья family.
items.explanation: К + dative for motion toward people. Друг is a family-plural masculine, so the dat pl is the irregular друзьям. Be careful: the gen / acc pl is друзей (with a different stem), but for the dative we use the regular family-pl ending -ьям.

items.promptEnglish: The teacher is helping the students.
items.hint: Помогать + dat. Студент is hard masc cons. Hard stems take which dat pl ending?
items.explanation: Помогать takes the dative. Студент is hard masculine consonant, so the dat pl ending is -ам: студентам. The same -ам ending appears on most hard stems, regardless of gender (журналам, книгам, окнам).

items.promptEnglish: The teacher is helping the girls.
items.hint: Девочка ends in velar к. Velars and hushers take which vowel by the spelling rule?
items.explanation: Девочка ends in the velar к. The 7-letter rule blocks -я after velars / hushers, so the dat pl ending becomes -ам (not -ям): девочкам. The same rule gives книгам, ручкам, чашкам.

items.promptEnglish: Masha tells stories to the children.
items.hint: Рассказывать takes acc (the thing told) + dat (the listener). Ребёнок → дети → ?
items.explanation: Рассказывать takes acc for the thing told (истории) and dat for the listener. Дети is the plural of ребёнок; the dat pl is детям, the soft ending on that stem.

items.promptEnglish: On Saturdays Masha helps the neighbors.
items.explanation: Помогать governs the dative: помогает соседям.

items.promptEnglish: Anton often writes letters to his teachers.
items.hint: Two objects: the letters (acc) and the recipients (dat).
items.explanation: Writing verbs take an accusative thing plus a dative recipient: пишет письма учителям.

items.promptEnglish: Lena calls her sisters every Sunday.
items.hint: Звонить + dative; note the second dative in 'по воскресеньям'.
items.explanation: Звонить takes a dative recipient: звонит сёстрам. The sentence stacks a second dative trigger: по + dative plural for the recurring day.

blanks: Учительница часто помогает _____. (The teacher often helps the pupils.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Помогать + dative plural. Ученик ends in the velar к, so the dat pl is -ам (not -ям): ученикам.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The nurse helps the doctors at the hospital.
errorCorrection.explanation: Врач is a hard-type stem (ч counts as unpaired), so the dative plural is -ам, not the soft -ям: помогает врачам. Врачям applies the soft ending where it does not belong and is not a valid form.

Сын builds its plural on сыновья, and the dative plural keeps the soft sign: звонит сыновьям. Сыновям drops the soft sign and is not a real spelling. Сынам applies the hard ending to the bare stem, skipping the -овь- extension entirely.

errorCorrection.sentence: По вечерах Лена гуляет в парке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the evenings Lena walks in the park.
errorCorrection.explanation: По in the habitual-time sense ('on evenings, every evening') governs the DATIVE plural: по вечерам. Вечерах is the prepositional plural, the look-alike a learner reaches for because -ах feels like the location ending, but по does not take the prepositional here. Remember по утрам, по вечерам, по выходным: all dative plural.

minimalPairs.explanation: Помогать takes the dative, not the accusative. Друзей is the gen/acc pl ('of friends'), but помогать requires the dative complement друзьям, with the -ьям family-pl ending.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha often calls her parents on weekends.
minimalPairs.explanation: Звонить takes the dative: 'to call someone' = звонить кому. The dat pl for this hard stem is -ам: родителям. Родителями is the instrumental plural ('with the parents'), which doesn't fit after звонить.

reviewVocab.definition: the dative plural; one ending across all three genders. Hard stems take -ам; soft stems take -ям.
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша помогает друзьям' слово 'друзьям' стоит в дательном падеже множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: the habitual-time construction. По + dat pl signals 'every X' / 'on Xs': по утрам (in the mornings), по вечерам (in the evenings), по выходным (on weekends), по понедельникам (on Mondays).
reviewVocab.example: Лена работает по утрам и отдыхает по выходным.

reviewVocab.definition: to help someone; помогать takes a dative complement, not an accusative. The dat pl ending is -ам / -ям: помогать друзьям, студентам, девочкам. The same dative pattern applies to звонить, писать ('to write to'), посылать, дарить, рассказывать.
